title: main red: `useLauncherApps-26838.test.tsx` intermittently sees a third app (Showcase) where it expects two; main push red at 08:30Z and 10:21Z
body:
triage#1 · os-zhuang · session_01AavokzJ5DndAwitDXvKy4U

Filing gate ①: main red, measured twice on `main` push runs. Main-red convention ①, so a p0 anchor. Filed by the triage seat (R728). ⛔ Not a claim.

## Measured

| Run | Head | Result |
|:--|:--|:--|
| push 40657300783 | `c4ad55ca` (08:30Z, #27049) | `Test UI (4/16)` red |
| push (next) | `74133d98` (08:38Z) | green |
| push 40671477651 | `4265176c` (10:21Z, the shared-record labels PR) | `Test UI (3/16)` red |

Both reds are the same assertion: `ui/packages/app-shell/src/hooks/__tests__/useLauncherApps-26838.test.tsx:100`, `expected [ …(3) ] to deeply equal [ …(2) ]`. A third entry `{ label: "Showcase", … }` appears beside `CRM`.

Neither head touches the launcher or the test. The test came in with `85c40fdf` (PR #27021, 08:04Z, #26838: "Home, the app switcher and launcher blocks offer only the apps /me/apps lists"). It passes on most runs, so it is **non-deterministic on main**. The likely shape is state shared across tests in the same shard (an app registry, a mocked `/me/apps` answer or a module cache that another test seeds with Showcase), not a product defect. The implementer measures which.

## Wanted

- Make the test own its input: a fresh registry or mock per test, reset in `beforeEach`/`afterEach`, and assert on exactly the apps it seeds. Then find which sibling test leaks Showcase and stop the leak at its source.
- ⛔ Never skip, retry-wrap or quarantine the test, and never loosen the assertion to `toContain`. The product rule (only the apps `/me/apps` lists) stays exactly as strict.
- Per the maintainer's 「同意，搭在 #27116 上做」, the test-authoring rule now owed on #27116's thread covers exactly this shape ("a test owns the data it asserts on").

## Reach

`Test UI` is now a required context, so a deterministic break could not land. This one passes the queue and then reds main pushes at random, and it will eject queue builds the same way.

Dedupe: open and closed issues searched for `useLauncherApps`: none. **New.**
